therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: radioligand binding to amyloid beta aggregates
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: in vivo detection of cerebral amyloid plaque burden
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: subjects previously imaged with florbetapir F 18 PET in trial 18F-AV-45-A07, followed to autopsy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: sensitivity and specificity of florbetapir-PET scan to detect moderate to frequent amyloid plaques at autopsy (CERAD criteria); Spearman correlation of PET image and amyloid plaque density by IHC

results.effect_size: Sensitivity 92% (95% CI: 78–98); Specificity 100% (95% CI: 80–100); Spearman correlation r=0.76 (95% CI: 0.62–0.85)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Spearman rank order correlation of florbetapir-PET median visual read vs. quantitative IHC amyloid plaque density across 6 brain regions = 0.76 (p<0.0001)
biomarker_changes: Florbetapir-PET positive (majority interpretation): 36 subjects with moderate/frequent plaques at autopsy
Florbetapir-PET negative (majority interpretation): 3 subjects with moderate/frequent plaques at autopsy (false negatives)
Florbetapir-PET positive (majority interpretation): 0 subjects with no/sparse plaques at autopsy (false positives)
Florbetapir-PET negative (majority interpretation): 20 subjects with no/sparse plaques at autopsy (true negatives)
Median sensitivity across 5 readers: 92% (95% CI: 69–95); Median specificity: 95% (95% CI: 90–100)
subgroup_findings: Sensitivity in subjects with autopsy within 1 year of scan: 96% (95% CI: 80–100)
Specificity in subjects with autopsy within 1 year of scan: 100% (95% CI: 78–100)
Reader 5 had the highest false negative rate (12 in all-autopsy population; 7 in within-1-year subgroup)

context.comparator: histopathological amyloid plaque assessment at autopsy (CERAD criteria)
context.duration: Follow-up to autopsy within 24 months of florbetapir PET scan
context.investigator_commentary: This is an autopsy follow-up extension study of trial 18F-AV-45-A07 (NCT00857415). No study drug was administered in this trial. Subjects previously dosed with florbetapir F 18 were followed to autopsy to validate PET imaging against histopathological gold standard.
